To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) QoE fairness is achieved with a small amount of App Net messages; (2) QoE gains depend on the number of App Net messages, the QoE fairness, and the network conditions; and (3) the QoE gains of App Net are higher than the gains of HAS.

(1) a coordinated HAS service can provide better QoE for heterogeneous clients compared to a standalone HAS service, and (2), the App Net mechanism with a client-side control decision can achieve the best QoE fairness and the lowest number of monitoring and controlling messages.

the App Net mechanism with the lowest complexity achieves the highest QoE gains, while the App Net mechanism that provides the highest fairness among heterogeneous clients achieves the lowest QoE gains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) a generic model of App Net mechanisms, (2) a methodology to quantitatively compare App Net mechanisms, and (3) a case study of the evaluation methodology for HAS.
the design and evaluation of a generic App Net framework that supports QoE management for multimedia applications.
a quantitative comparison of the App Net mechanisms for HAS, which will be extended to other multimedia applications and network scenarios in future work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed evaluation methodology can be applied to other applications, and can provide a solid basis for further App Net studies.
the App Net mechanisms are able to achieve better QoE than the baseline HAS, while the complexity of AppNet implementation is manageable.
App Net is a promising mechanism for QoE management, and that App Net mechanisms are able to provide a fair QoE distribution among heterogeneous clients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) App Net mechanisms are able to achieve a better QoE fairness compared to the baseline HAS, (2) a higher level of App Net coordination results in a better QoEs, (3) a higher level App Net coordination requires a higher number of monitoring and coordination messages, and (4) a higher level coordination results in more complex App Net implementation.
App Net mechanisms can be beneficial in terms of achieving better QoE for all clients.
App Net can improve QoE of HAS services in terms of video quality and QoE distribution, but the QoE gain is at the cost of a higher network load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, the more complex the App Net mechanism, the higher the QoE gains.
, in order to improve the QoE fairness, it is necessary to coordinate the control actions among the clients.

, for the considered HAS case study, the App Net mechanisms that are based on a local view of network conditions and that do not involve any coordination between the applications and network are able to achieve similar QoE gains as the mechanisms that are based a global view and that include coordination between the applications.
